questions.question: In 2026, a scrap yard is the final processor for household refrigerators charged with R-134a, a non-exempt substitute refrigerant. Does the safe disposal section, 40 CFR 82.155, apply to them?

options.A: No, because the section applies only to appliances containing class I and class II refrigerants
options.B: Only if each refrigerator holds more than five pounds of refrigerant
options.C: Yes, because starting on January 1, 2018, it applies to appliances containing any class I or class II refrigerant or any non-exempt substitute refrigerant
options.D: Only if the refrigerators were manufactured before 2018

questions.explanation: "Starting on January 1, 2018, this section applies to disposal of appliances containing any class I or class II refrigerant or any non-exempt substitute refrigerant." The class I and class II limit applied only until that date.

questions.question: Under the definitions, what does it mean to recover refrigerant?

options.A: To clean refrigerant for reuse in equipment of the same owner through oil separation and filter-driers
options.B: To reprocess refrigerant to all of the specifications in appendix A
options.C: To remove refrigerant in any condition from an appliance and store it in an external container without necessarily testing or processing it
options.D: To release refrigerant from an appliance in a controlled way
